rochdale.snapshot: Rochdale sits inside the Greater Manchester full-fibre build, and its telecoms trade splits two ways. The build contractors and structured-cabling firms running crews across the town tend to buy through trade accounts with branded kit for whole teams, while the ex-BT sole traders and one-van broadband and CCTV installers order direct online with no account. We serve both routes side by side, fleet and single installer alike.
rochdale.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Rochdale and Greater Manchester
s1loc: Rochdale is in the middle of a heavy full-fibre build. CityFibre is delivering a 30 million pound town-wide network through contractor Network Plus, Openreach has invested around 13 million pound and reached roughly 80 percent of properties, and alt-nets including Netomnia and YouFibre are pushing fibre-to-the-premises alongside, with Heywood and the surrounding townships drawn into the rollout too. Engineers from the major fibre and mobile networks work the streets and cabinets across districts like Castleton, Norden, Bamford, Spotland and Milnrow, with civils crews and delivery partners trenching and pulling fibre right across the borough.

Off the residential rollout sits a steady commercial scene. Structured-cabling and CCTV installers wire offices, schools and warehouses in Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre across Kingsway Business Park, Stakehill Industrial Estate and the town-centre Riverside development, while units around Queensway and the Rochdale Exchange keep local installers busy. The mix runs from multi-site contractors fitting whole business parks to one-van engineers handling a single shopfront camera system, and all of them need hard-wearing branded workwear for work across the borough's premises.
